layers.message: Add export audit trail to scope

graderOnly: After the final-deliverable review was committed, a later commit ('Add export audit trail to scope') rewrote the scope's work item 2 so that AC-002 now means 'every export is recorded in the service log with the requesting user's id, the filters applied, and the export file name'. AC-002 previously meant 'an export request from a non-administrator or no signed-in user is rejected by server-side authorization before any export file is written'.

The scope has no Retired Acceptance Identifiers section and no record of the earlier AC-002 meaning; the identifier was reused for a materially different condition instead of being retired and replaced with a new identifier.

The technical design, development plan, verification report, implementation review, documentation record, and final-deliverable review all use the earlier (administrator-only access) meaning of AC-002, and all cite the scope blob from before the edit, which no longer matches the current scope.
The administrator-only access obligation, still stated in the scope's Goal and Constraints and in Active Work.Request, is now represented by no current acceptance condition.
The implementation writes no export log; nothing in src/ logs exports.
The correct owner of the defect is Scoper (FailureType SCOPING); sign-off readiness is not established.

all.why: Synchronizer must not rewrite scope wording or acceptance identifiers
sign-off readiness must not be declared; routed to Scoper or held in SYNCHRONIZING
the skill persists every unresolved discrepancy in the synchronization record before routing
the synchronization gate cannot pass with an unresolved acceptance identity discrepancy

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Synchronizer owns only its record and routes defects; it does not change implementation, documentation, or other roles' records

selfChecks.why: the reused identifier is not mechanically detectable; the state is valid for check

selfChecks.cmd: pnpm --filter export test && pnpm --filter export test:integration
selfChecks.why: the implementation and its tests are unchanged and pass

selfChecks.cmd: s=.standards/docs/scope/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && grep -qF -e '- `AC-002`: Every export is recorded in the service log' $s && test $(grep -c '^- `AC-00[1-3]`: ' $s) -eq 3 && ! grep -q 'Retired Acceptance' $s && ! grep -q 'Previous Cycles' $s && ! grep -qF 'rejected by server-side authorization' $s && git show HEAD~1:$s | grep -qF 'rejected by server-side authorization before any export file is written'
selfChecks.why: AC-002 now carries a different meaning, the earlier meaning was dropped, and no retirement history exists

selfChecks.cmd: a=.standards/docs/specs/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && grep -qF -e '- `AC-002`: `requireAdmin` as the handler' $a && grep -qF 'AC-002 / no user gets 401' .standards/docs/verification/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && grep -qF 'AC-002 / no user 401' .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md
selfChecks.why: downstream design and reports use the earlier AC-002 meaning

selfChecks.cmd: s=.standards/docs/scope/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && old=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1:$s) && new=$(git rev-parse HEAD:$s) && test $old != $new && for f in .standards/docs/verification/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/implementation.md .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md .standards/docs/documentation/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md; do grep -q $old $f || exit 1; done && ! grep -rq $new .standards/docs
selfChecks.why: every report cites the pre-edit scope blob; none cites the current scope content
the implementation records no export log

selfChecks.cmd: test "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = 'Add export audit trail to scope' && test "$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD)" = .standards/docs/scope/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && ! git status --porcelain | grep -q . && test ! -e .standards/docs/synchronization
selfChecks.why: the only change after the final review is the scope edit; tree clean; no synchronization record yet
state is SYNCHRONIZING with no recovery, obligations, or blocker

notes: Built on export-synchronizing (cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 at SYNCHRONIZING, all upstream records COMPLETE, no synchronization record). One overlay commit, 'Add export audit trail to scope', edits only the scope record: work item 2 becomes 'Export audit trail' and AC-002 is reused for a materially different condition (every export recorded in the service log with user id, filters, file name). No Retired Acceptance Identifiers section is added, so the earlier AC-002 meaning (non-admin/anonymous export rejected before any file is written) leaves no trace in the scope, while the Goal, Constraints, and Active Work.Request still state the admin-only obligation. STATE.md is unchanged (FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL). The design, plan, verification, both reviews, and documentation record keep the earlier meaning and cite the pre-edit scope blob via the base's BLOB placeholders, so the scope's content identity no longer matches any report. check.mjs cannot detect meaning reuse and passes. Compromise: because base layers are fixed, the scope change can only appear as a commit after final review (effectively an edit outside a legal transition); a correct Synchronizer detects it from identity mismatch and routes it to Scoper.
